back: A simple method, like naive or seasonal naive, that your model must beat. It sets the bar and shows your lift.
Training must use only the past. A random split lets the model see the future and gives scores that are too good.
Using information in training or features that will not be available at prediction time. It inflates offline scores.
Mean, variance and autocorrelation stay the same over time. Many classic models assume it.
It subtracts the previous value. It removes a trend and helps make a series stationary.
The correlation between a series and its own lagged copy, for each lag. It reveals seasonality and memory.
The correlation at lag k after removing the effect of shorter lags. It helps pick the AR order.
MAE is the average absolute error and is easy to read. RMSE squares errors, so big errors count more.

front: Why does MAPE fail near zero?
back: It divides by the actual. Zero is undefined and tiny actuals give huge percentages.
Sum of absolute errors divided by sum of actuals. It weights errors by volume and handles small actuals better than MAPE.
Test MAE divided by the in-sample MAE of a naive forecast. A value below 1 means better than naive.
Despite its name it is not symmetric, and it is unstable when actual and forecast are both near zero.
Evaluating a method at several past forecast origins, each time training on the past only and scoring the next horizon.
Expanding keeps all history from the start. Sliding keeps a fixed length and drops the oldest data.
The last time point whose data the model may use. The forecast is for times after it.
One model predicts one step ahead and feeds its own forecast back as input. Errors can accumulate.
Train a separate model for each horizon step. No error feedback, but more models and less shared learning.
Local fits one model per series. Global fits one model on many series and shares patterns.
A forecast of a chosen percentile, such as the 90th. The actual should fall below it 90% of the time.
The loss for quantile forecasts. It penalises under- and over-forecast with different weights set by q.
The share of actual values that fall inside the interval. A 90% interval should cover about 90%.
A method that uses past errors on a calibration set to build intervals with a coverage guarantee under mild assumptions.
The forecast equals the value from the same point in the last season, such as the same weekday last week.
New level = alpha × latest actual + (1 − alpha) × old level. Alpha near 1 reacts fast.
Error, Trend, Seasonality: a family of exponential smoothing models with additive or multiplicative parts.

front: When is ARIMA a good choice?
back: A single series or few series, short history, clear autocorrelation, and a need for intervals and an interpretable model.
A method for intermittent demand. It smooths the size of non-zero demands and the gap between them separately.
Adjusting forecasts at different levels so they add up, for example stores sum to region.
It handles many features, non-linear effects and many series in one global model, and trains fast. Needs careful lag features.

front: Give three feature types for GBM forecasting.
back: Lags, rolling statistics, and calendar features (weekday, month, holiday). Add known-future covariates like price or promotion.
A feature whose future values are known at forecast time, such as holidays, planned promotions or price plans.
The link between inputs and target changes over time. The model's error rises even if inputs look the same.
The distribution of the inputs changes compared with training. It is a warning sign, not proof of worse accuracy.

front: Name two ways to detect an anomaly.
back: Z-score or robust MAD on residuals, and a forecast-interval check. Isolation Forest is a model-based option.
A time where the statistical behaviour of a series, like its mean, shifts. CUSUM and PELT find them.
Stock at the quantile equal to under-cost / (under-cost + over-cost). It turns a quantile forecast into an order.
Error of a baseline minus error after a process step. It shows if each step helps or hurts.

front: What is a foundation model for time series?
back: A large model pre-trained on many series that forecasts new series zero-shot, such as Chronos or TimesFM.

front: Name a leakage trap in rolling features.
back: A rolling mean that includes the current row. Shift by one step first, then roll.
An average hides failures. Segments by store, product, or volume show where the model is weak.

front: What does a cold start mean?
back: A new series with little or no history. Use group averages, similar items, or a global model with static features.

front: How to explain a forecast to a manager?
back: State the number, the range, the main driver, and the decision it supports. Avoid jargon and show one chart.
